title: Phytohormone Profiling by Liquid Chromatography Coupled to Mass Spectrometry
author: Camilo E. Vital
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.zgff3tn

steps.title: Sample Collection and Preparation
steps.instruction: Collect plant tissue samples and prepare them for extraction while maintaining cryogenic conditions.

substeps.instruction: Immediately freeze samples in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C until use.
Macerate samples in liquid nitrogen using a mortar and pestle without allowing them to thaw.
Weigh approximately 110mg of each sample into 2ml microtubes and annotate the weight for absolute quantification.
Alternatively, weigh samples into 1.5ml round-bottom Eppendorf tubes and macerate using glass or tungsten beads at 25 Hz/s for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Phytohormone Extraction
steps.instruction: Extract phytohormones from the plant tissue using a solvent mixture and sonication.

substeps.instruction: Add 400μl of a solution containing methanol:isopropanol:acetic acid (20:79:1).
Vortex samples 4 times for 20 seconds each while keeping on ice.
Sonicate for 10 minutes, let stand on ice for 30 minutes, and sonicate again for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge at 13,000g for 10 minutes at 4ºC and collect supernatants in new tubes.
Repeat the addition of solvent, vortexing/sonication, and centrifugation on the remaining pellet to obtain a second supernatant.
Pool the supernatants from both extractions.
Centrifuge the pooled samples at 20,000g for 5 minutes at 4ºC to remove debris.
Collect approximately 600μl of the supernatant into new tubes.
Filter the supernatant using a disposable 0.2ml PVDF membrane.
Store samples at -80ºC until LC-MS analysis.

steps.title: Standard Curve Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare standard solutions and optimize the mass spectrometer for quantification.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a standard solution containing 1.0 ug/mL of each compound in methanol:isopropanol:acetic acid (20:79:1) and transfer to vials.
Setup a product ion scan method for each compound to optimize transmission and fragmentation parameters (manually or automatically).
Use a second transition to confirm the first transition for quantification, particularly for low intensity signals.
Select the higher intensity fragment ions to compose the MRM (Multiple Reaction Monitoring) transition list.
Prepare serial dilutions from 0.1 ng/mL up to 400 ng/mL in duplicate, based on instrument sensitivity and linearity.
Inject 5.0 ul of standards and perform the MRM method.
Generate XIC (extracted ion chromatogram) areas for each dilution using Skyline software.
Export XICs to Microsoft Excel.
Generate linear curves of XIC area versus phytohormone concentration (ng/mL) to determine concentration in fresh tissue.

steps.title: LC-MS System Configuration
steps.instruction: Configure the UHPLC and Triple Quadrupole Mass Spectrometer (QQQ) settings.

substeps.instruction: Use a UHPLC system with 1mL vials and a 5μl injection loop.
Equip the system with a Zorbax SB-C18 guard column (1.8 μm) and an analytical Zorbax Eclipse Plus C18 column (1.8 μm, 2.1 x 50mm).
Prepare mobile phases: Buffer A (water with 0.02% acetic acid) and Buffer B (acetonitrile with 0.02% acetic acid).
Set the gradient (%B): 5% at 0-1 min; 60% at 11 min; 95% at 13-17 min; 5% at 19-20 min.
Set solvent flow rate to 0.3ml/min and column temperature to 30ºC.
Configure ESI (Electrospray Ionization) settings: gas temperature 300ºC, nitrogen flow rate 10L/min, nebulizer pressure 35psi, and capillary voltage 4000V.
Operate the mass spectrometer in positive or negative mode depending on the specific phytohormone detection method.

steps.title: Sample Analysis and Quantification
steps.instruction: Inject samples and calculate the final phytohormone concentration.

substeps.instruction: Inject all samples randomly using the MRM method used for the standard curves.
Analyze raw mass spectra using Skyline software to generate XIC areas.
Export XIC areas to Microsoft Excel.
Convert XIC areas to ng/mL using the previously generated standard linear curves.
Convert ng/mL to ng/g of fresh tissue based on the initial sample weight (e.g., 110mg) and final volume.

steps.title: Skyline Software Data Processing
steps.instruction: Process the raw LC-MS data using Skyline software for peak area extraction.

substeps.instruction: Create a transition list in OpenOffice and import it into a blank Skyline document via Edit > Insert > Transition List.
Configure transition settings for QqQ mass spectrometry and save the project.
Import results from .d files generated by the LC/MS QqQ.
Use 'View > Retention Times > Replicate Comparison' and 'View > Peak Areas > Replicate Comparison' to review data.
Manually edit and correct the selected chromatogram areas by moving the dashed line on the RT bar for all compounds and samples.
Export the peak areas of all XICs as a spreadsheet file via File > Export > Report > Transition Result.
